title: Shifted Tate-line endomorphisms on a connected geometric scheme
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $N\ge1$ invertible in $k$, and $B$ a commutative $\mathbf Z/N$-algebra. Let $Y$ be a nonempty connected $k$-scheme [def-weil-connected-scheme]. On its small etale site let $B_Y(1)=\mu_{N,Y}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}B_Y$ and $L=B_Y(r)[d]$ for integers $r\ge0$ and $d$, with tensor-power Tate twist [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] and derived shift in [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Give $D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ and $D((\operatorname{Spec}k)_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ the $B$-linear structure induced from their abelian categories of $B$-module sheaves [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category]. Then the scalar map
$$B\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B)}(L),\qquad b\longmapsto b\,1_L$$
is a bijection. In particular, for any $B$-linear functor [def-weil-linear-category] $G:D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B)\to D((\operatorname{Spec}k)_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ and any isomorphism $G(L)\cong B_{\operatorname{Spec}k}$, an endomorphism $v:L\to L$ is an isomorphism whenever $G(v)$ is an isomorphism. Here $B$-linear means $G(bf)=bG(f)$ on every morphism group.

proof.text: Apply [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] with $A=B$, $m=N$, $T=Y$: $NB=0$, and $N$ is invertible on $Y$ because it is invertible in $k$. Thus $F=B_Y(r)$ is locally free of rank one over $B_Y$. The shifts of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] cancel: applying $[-d]$ to a map $F[d]\to F[d]$ and $[d]$ to a map $F\to F$ gives inverse correspondences, preserving composition, and they preserve scalar multiplication because the shift functors are $B$-linear [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category]. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], maps between these degree-zero sheaves in the derived category are exactly module-sheaf maps. Choose local bases $e_i$ on an etale trivializing cover $U_i\to Y$. A module-sheaf endomorphism $f$ is uniquely given on $U_i$ by $f(e_i)=a_i e_i$, $a_i\in B_Y(U_i)$, since on every further etale restriction $f(te_i)=t f(e_i)$. On $U_i\times_YU_j$ write $e_j=u_{ij}e_i$ with $u_{ij}$ a unit (the inverse change of basis supplies its inverse). Linearity gives $a_j u_{ij}=u_{ij}a_i$, hence $a_j=a_i$ by commutativity and cancellation of the unit. The sheaf axiom for $B_Y$ glues the $a_i$ to a unique $a\in B_Y(Y)$. Conversely each such $a$ acts on $F$, so this gives the scalar bijection $\Gamma(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B_Y)\to\operatorname{End}_{D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B)}(L)$. Addition, composition and the identity become addition, multiplication and $1$ of sections by the same basis calculation.

proof.text: The underlying additive sheaf of rings $B_Y$ is the constant sheaf with value the abelian group $(B,+)$. Since $Y$ is nonempty and connected, [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-connected] identifies its global sections with $B$, and the identification is induced by the constant-section map. The local calculation in Step 1 is compatible with addition and multiplication, so it upgrades to a ring isomorphism $B\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{End}_{D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B)}(L)$, exactly the displayed scalar map. This proves the first assertion, including the zero ring and the case $r=0$.

proof.text: Let $G$ and $v$ be as in the second assertion. By the $B$-linearity in [def-weil-linear-category] of $G$ between the $B$-linear categories of [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category], and Step 2, write $v=b\,1_L$ and obtain $G(v)=b\,1_{G(L)}$. Transporting along the chosen isomorphism $G(L)\cong B_{\operatorname{Spec}k}$ gives the scalar endomorphism $b\,1_{B_{\operatorname{Spec}k}}$. Apply Steps 1–2 to the nonempty connected scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$: its endomorphism ring is $B$, so the inverse of this scalar endomorphism corresponds to some $c\in B$ and satisfies $bc=1=cb$. Thus $b$ is a unit in $B$.

proof.text: The scalar map $c\mapsto c\,1_L$ is multiplicative, and the scalar corresponding to $b^{-1}$ is a two-sided inverse to $v=b\,1_L$. Hence $v$ is an isomorphism whenever $G(v)$ is an isomorphism.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q98-e6a7eba45 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, every cited statement, the unit route, the parent lem-coef-finite-dualizing (steps 3 and 5), Stacks 06XS (derived.tex l.8713-8727) and 03P5 (etale-cohomology.tex l.2437-2456), and the blueprint master parent paragraph 'The Tate rank-one object' (l.47-58, and its main-20261015 copy). That paragraph does not contain the scalar argument, so the agent-written proof origin is correct. The statement is true: End(B_Y(r)[d]) = End of an invertible B_Y-module = Gamma(Y,B_Y), which is B on a connected Y. I tested B=0, N=1, r=0, d of both signs, Y=Spec k and Y=A^r. Connectedness and nonemptiness are both needed: two points give B x B, and the empty scheme breaks injectivity. In step 1 the local-basis gluing (a_j u_ij = u_ij a_i, so a_j = a_i) is correct. Step 2 is correct: the connected-sections node holds for any abelian group, and the module structure goes through the same constant-section map. Step 3 applies the already-proved first assertion on Spec k, so it is not circular. No duplicate exists: lem-pur-lisse-rank-one-aut covers only finite-stage pro-etale sheaves on separated finite-type schemes. No new nodes and no SGA. Three faults, all repaired in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/lem-coef-connected-tate-line-endomorphisms.json. (1) B3/C4: the statement's b*1_L and 'B-linear functor' use the B-linear structure of the derived categories with no node for it. I added a citation to the on-route Mathlib leaf lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category (DerivedCategory.instLinear, instLinearShiftFunctorInt) and added it to stmt_deps; the meaning is unchanged.
